quests.conceptTitle: Pre-Reading Schema Activation: The Night Market Returns
quests.passage: After a three-year break, the Dockside Night Market reopens this Friday with more than sixty stalls. The market will run every Friday and Saturday from 5 p.m. until midnight through September. quests.passage: I read with interest your article on the proposed bike lane along Hartley Road. Critics say it will remove twelve parking spaces and hurt local shops. But when I shop on Hartley Road I rarely drive, and most customers I see arrive on foot or by bike. Perhaps the question isn't how many parking spaces we will lose, but how many customers a safer street might bring. I'd urge the council to run a six-month trial before deciding.

quests.conceptTitle: Pre-Reading Schema Activation: The Watch
quests.passage: When my grandfather died, the only thing I asked for was his watch, which hadn't worked for decades. The first repairer said the mechanism was too old; the second quoted a price I couldn't afford. It was the third, a woman working above a shoe shop, who opened the case, sighed, and said she'd see what she could do. Two weeks later she called. The watch ran, but four minutes slow each day, and she apologized for that. I told her I wouldn't change it for the world.

If you can't pay the full balance each month, paying even slightly more than the minimum shortens the time you're in debt.

A class offers that interaction and a teacher who notices your particular mistakes, but it demands a fixed schedule and a bigger budget. Many learners therefore combine the two, using an app for daily vocabulary and a weekly class for conversation.

A fund-raising drive then collected $240,000, which covered most of the repairs, and the council agreed to pay the rest. Workers replaced the floor and rebuilt the stage in the autumn. The first show will be a children's play, chosen because the theatre's founder always said it should belong to the whole town.
